subject.title: Sub-agent startup silence: no first-progress signal, aborted runs appear as hangs

question: Should OpenClaw add explicit sub-agent lifecycle phases such as `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed`, or solve startup silence using the existing lifecycle/error surface?
rationale: The source-repro is strong, but the fix creates a cross-surface core event contract with compatibility and product semantics that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Adopt typed lifecycle phases
options.body: Accept the additive event contract and replace the stale PR with a current-main implementation that updates producer, consumers, SDK normalization, docs, and proof together.

options.title: Use existing phases with richer metadata
options.body: Avoid new phase strings and instead carry startup/progress state through existing lifecycle events and terminal metadata, with tests for unknown-consumer behavior.

options.title: Defer to narrower sandbox/startup bugs
options.body: Keep this issue open but require a maintainer to split specific startup-abort causes such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39248 before adding a general lifecycle contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt typed lifecycle phases
recommendation.body: Accept the additive event contract and replace the stale PR with a current-main implementation that updates producer, consumers, SDK normalization, docs, and proof together.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points to steipete as the strongest current routing candidate for terminal outcome and gateway/session lifecycle contract decisions.
